columns.rationale: null_rate is 0.0 across 16 rows and distinct_count is 16, so every row carries a unique two-letter IATA carrier code such as '9E', 'AA', and 'WN'; retained as text because the codes are alphanumeric.
null_rate is 0.0 and distinct_count is 16, matching the row_count of 16; distinct_values such as 'Delta Air Lines Inc.' and 'Virgin America' are free-text carrier names kept as VARCHAR.
Profile marks this column is_airbyte_metadata: true; its 16 distinct UUID-shaped values are capture-tool identifiers, not business data.
Profile marks this column is_airbyte_metadata: true and distinct_count is 1 with min equal to max ('2026-09-02T23:26:17'), so it records a single capture moment rather than business content.
Profile marks this column is_airbyte_metadata: true and distinct_count is 1 with the only value '{}', so it carries no business information.

decisions.rationale: dataset.duplicate_row_rate is 0.0 over a row_count of 16, so bronze holds no exact duplicate rows and no dedupe step is proposed.
carrier has distinct_count 16 equal to row_count 16 with null_rate 0.0, so the IATA code identifies one row per airline; name is equally distinct but codes are the stable join key to flight data.
_airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at, and _airbyte_meta all carry is_airbyte_metadata: true and are dropped as pipeline capture columns.
Both business columns landed as VARCHAR and their distinct_values are alphanumeric codes and free-text names, so no cast to a numeric or temporal type is supported by the evidence.
carrier and name each report null_count 0 and null_rate 0.0, so both are proposed required with null_handling not_applicable.

purpose: silver_nyc_airlines is the cleaned airline reference dimension derived from bronze.nyc_airlines: one row per IATA carrier code with its full airline name, feeding joins from flight-level fact tables that carry only the two-letter carrier code.
usage: Join on carrier to resolve a two-letter code to a display name. The table is a small static lookup of 16 rows, so consumers should expect it to change only when the upstream carrier list changes; read name as the human-facing label and carrier as the key.
limitations: The profile covers only 16 rows with duplicate_row_rate 0.0, so uniqueness of carrier is asserted from that small snapshot and must be re-measured in the warehouse before approval. No capture timestamp is retained because the only available one (_airbyte_extracted_at, distinct_count 1) is pipeline metadata, so this table carries no load-time lineage column and no historical versioning of airline names.
